description: Portable processor scenarios for OpenAPI decisions sharpened during the 0.2.0 review. Configuration is named semantically; adapters normalize HTTP observations.

scenarios.description: A later patch-looking OpenAPI edition is refused at load instead of accepted by version-line inference.
A scalar query parameter uses the OpenAPI-declared query location and serialization rather than becoming a body field.
Same-named path and query parameters remain independently writable through the first candidate's routed source representation.
Two declared JSON-family request media are preserved as alternatives; the corpus lists both without preference.
An operation with no concrete success-response media omits Accept instead of inventing application/json.
A 201 response uses the default declaration for response media/decode but remains successful because classification is independently 2xx.
The same default declaration may describe a 404 body but never upgrades that non-2xx status into success.

Several effective servers require explicit selection; array order does not create an OpenBindings default. A missing selection is missing consumer configuration (ruled 2026-08-13, R1+R5): the invocation challenges CONTEXT_REQUIRED (config.value, point server) through the retryable context negotiation — the same lane as a missing request-media selection — and nothing dispatches.
A header credential colliding with an effective header parameter is refused even when caller input omits the parameter; one artifact declaration never silently supplies the other.
An API-key credential targeting processor-owned Accept cannot replace response-media negotiation and is refused before dispatch.
A request-body schema reached through $ref and allOf is resolved before flattening; its declared property becomes a body field rather than a synthetic body wrapper.
A media type declared for a different success status cannot govern the actual response.
Request-body flattening uses each Media Type Object's own schema: a parameter-colliding candidate is excluded without poisoning a distinct non-colliding artifact alternative.
An OAS header parameter named Authorization is ignored by the artifact's own rule: it creates neither a required input nor a wire header.
Two OAS-distinct header parameters that differ only by case collide on HTTP's case-insensitive field channel and remain unresolvable.
Two content-map keys that differ textually but denote the same parsed media type are a normalized collision, never first-key selection.
A response media declaration with matching parameters outranks its unparameterized sibling while additional actual parameters remain admissible.
Two distinct response declarations tying at the greatest matching parameter specificity are a protocol error rather than content-map order precedence.
A 303 response is not followed by rewriting the artifact-bound POST to GET; it remains the final non-2xx failure response.
The first patch-looking edition beyond the accepted OpenAPI 3.0 set is refused rather than inferred compatible.
An envelope-shaped application object remains ordinary body data because the private routed representation is a structurally disjoint one-tuple.

A location-backed multi-document description resolves an external Path Item and Security Scheme, and fragment-only Parameter, Request Body, and Response references inside the external document stay scoped to that document.
Security Requirement Objects are alternatives: when two complete alternatives are available, invocation selects exactly one and never unions their credentials onto the wire.
Credentials are never volunteered when the effective operation declares no security requirement.
A raw Cookie header parameter cannot coexist with a structured cookie parameter, even when the caller omits both; cookie assembly never silently overwrites an artifact declaration.
An effective Host header parameter cannot replace processor-owned target resolution and is refused before dispatch even when omitted by the caller.
An effective Content-Length header parameter cannot replace processor-owned body framing and is refused before dispatch even when omitted by the caller.
An OAS 3.0 binary schema carries exact raw bytes for a concrete image media type; the lane is schema-driven rather than restricted to application/octet-stream.
A non-canonical Base64 boundary value for an OAS 3.0 raw body refuses before dispatch.
Raw-body bytes are declaration-selected and never sniffed as JSON merely because their decoded spelling is JSON text.
A required raw body with no caller input refuses before dispatch like every other required request body.
An OAS 3.1 schema-omitted image body uses the OpenBindings Base64 boundary and emits raw bytes.
An OAS 3.1 contentEncoding string is transferred as encoded text and is not decoded as OpenBindings boundary Base64.
A required range-only object body challenges for requestMedia during preflight before input consumption and performs zero dispatch; object shape does not imply JSON.
A configured application/json concrete type instantiates a wildcard declaration while the operation input remains a pure application object.
An exact media declaration outranks type and universal ranges for a configured concrete request media type.
A type range outranks a universal range for a configured concrete request media type.
A configured concrete media type covered by a range still refuses when the first candidate defines no encoder for that governing schema and media combination.
A configured text/plain concrete type covered by a wildcard refuses when the governing schema and supplied value are objects.
An optional range-only request body with no caller value bypasses media selection and emits neither a body nor Content-Type.
An optional range-only body supplied without prior requestMedia refuses after input is present rather than issuing an unsafe replay challenge.
An OAS 3.0 binary success response crosses the protocol-independent output boundary as canonical Base64 of its exact octets.
The actual concrete response media selects an OAS 3.1 range, whose schema-omitted body preserves exact bytes as Base64.
A concrete application/json response selected through application/* still emits the parsed JSON application value.
A successful text/event-stream response selected through a declared wildcard retains server-streaming lifecycle and per-event values.
An explicitly dynamic form object rides as one routed application value, preserving a body member independently from a same-named query parameter.
An OAS 3.1 pattern property selects the effective schema and application/json default for its dynamic multipart member.
A declaration-complex exact JSON body rides as one routed application value; no branch or body field is selected by the binding.
An exact schema-omitted OAS 3.0 non-JSON declaration carries request and response octets through the canonical Base64 application boundary.

A single-non-null-branch choice part carries its branch's serialization. This scenario also asserted, until 2026-08-17, that an unconstrained part beside it takes its OAS per-type default from the value's JSON application type — at `openapi: 3.1.2`, whose Encoding Object default table states application/octet-stream for a part whose `type` is absent. That half was wrong and moved to OAPI-PS-56 (the 3.0 line, where the convention applies) and OAPI-PS-57 (the refusal the 3.1 line requires).

A urlencoded property whose Encoding Object declares none of style, explode or allowReserved takes the OAS's content-based path, which the OAS pairs with RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1; a space therefore rides as +. The OAS also records that percent-encoding it as %20 satisfies the media type, so both spellings are permitted observations and neither is this specification's preference.

expected.description: RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1: space characters are replaced by +.
OAS 3.1.2 Section 4.8.12.4 records that %20 also meets the media type's requirements.

scenarios.description: The same property with an Encoding Object declaring style takes the OAS's style-based path, which the OAS pairs with RFC 6570 and notes "does not use + for form-urlencoded"; a space therefore rides as %20. The two paths spelling a space differently is incorporation, not divergence.

expected.description: RFC 6570 expansion percent-encodes the space, and the OAS states of this path that it "does not use + for form-urlencoded". One permitted observation, not a set.

scenarios.description: Path selection inside an urlencoded body is by an Encoding Object field's explicit PRESENCE, not by its value. OAS 3.0.4/3.1.1/3.1.2 say "the presence of at least one of style, explode, or allowReserved with an explicit value is equivalent to using schema with in: \"query\" Parameter Objects", and OAS 3.1.0 says of each field "If a value is explicitly defined, then the value of contentType (implicit or explicit) SHALL be ignored." allowReserved: false restates the field's own default, so it is an explicit value and takes the style path.

expected.description: An engine that reads truthiness rather than presence puts this property on the content path and emits note=one+two. One permitted observation, not a set.

scenarios.description: OAS 3.0.4 is the edition where the 3.0 line first states the content interpretation ("The absence of all three of those fields is the equivalent of using content") and where Appendix E first appears. An urlencoded property with no Encoding Object therefore takes the content path there, which the OAS pairs with RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1, whose first escaping step replaces a space with +. OAS 3.0.0-3.0.3 state neither sentence and this specification states no path-selection rule for that line, so no scenario pins it.

expected.description: The 3.0 line reaches the content path from 3.0.4 onward. One permitted observation, not a set.

scenarios.description: An array-valued multipart property takes its per-part default Content-Type from its ITEMS schema, never from the array. Every accepted OAS edition states this, in one of two ways. The Encoding Object's contentType default says "for array – the default is defined based on the inner type" (3.0.0–3.0.3, 3.1.0), "according to the type and format of the items schema" (3.0.4), "according to the type of the items schema" (3.1.1, 3.1.2). Independently, the multipart guidance in 3.0.0–3.0.3 and 3.1.0 says "If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain". A string items schema with no contentEncoding therefore reaches text/plain on every edition, and each element takes its own part. An engine that keyed the default on the array itself would emit ONE part carrying the whole JSON array, which is what the per-element body assertions below exclude. The per-part Content-Type header is deliberately NOT asserted: [RFC7578] Section 4.4, which 3.1.1 incorporates, says "Each part MAY have an (optional) 'Content-Type' header field, which defaults to 'text/plain'", so emitting it and omitting it are both inside the permitted set and requiring either would invent a preference the authority does not state.

expected.description: Two parts named tags, each carrying one item as its whole body. An array-keyed default would put ["alpha","beta"] in one part and match neither body assertion.

scenarios.description: On the 3.0 line no accepted edition states a default contentType row that reaches a part declaring no `type` — 3.0.0 through 3.0.3 enumerate a string with format binary, other primitive types, object, and array without a catch-all, and 3.0.4 tabulates the same cases keyed on a declared type. openbindings.openapi@1 answers there with its own convention, keying the per-type default from the supplied value's JSON application type, so an object value rides as an application/json part.

OAS 3.1.1 tabulates the Encoding Object default contentType for a part whose `type` is absent as application/octet-stream, in the first row of that field's own table, and openbindings.openapi@1 defines no boundary from a JSON application value to octets for a form part. The multipart alternative is therefore not a carriage candidate, and with no other alternative the invocation refuses before dispatch rather than guessing a lane. OAS 3.1.0 reaches the same answer through the total catch-all closing its prose enumeration, and OAS 3.1.2 carries 3.1.1's row verbatim.

A multipart property declared as an array, supplied a value that is not an array, refuses before dispatch. §9.2 says of the form-serialization lanes that "An invalid value or a member for which the resolved schema leaves no faithful form carriage refuses before dispatch." The declaration is what decides this part's carriage — an array property rides as one part per element, which OAPI-PS-55 pins — so a value carrying no elements has no faithful form carriage at all. The failure mode this excludes is silent: a processor that falls back to the WHOLE-property schema serializes the invalid value into one application/json part, the artifact's own declaration never described that part, and the caller is told nothing. Refusing is also the only outcome that keeps the two lanes agreeing, since the same processor refuses the declaration outright when the declared schema leaves no carriage.

expected.description: No request is emitted. A processor keying the part on the whole-property schema instead would dispatch one application/json part carrying "alpha".

scenarios.description: A multipart part whose resolved Schema Object declares a non-string type and also carries `contentEncoding` keeps its own per-type default row. Every accepted 3.1 edition keys the application/octet-stream row on a declared string — 3.1.0 as "a `type: string` with a `contentEncoding`", 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 as the Encoding Object default table's `string` row with contentEncoding present — while the `number, integer, or boolean` row holds `n/a` in the contentEncoding column, which that table's own note defines as "the presence or value of contentEncoding is irrelevant". The incorporated dialect says the same independently: JSON Schema 2020-12 makes the Content vocabulary annotations that "do not function as validation assertions" and conditions both `contentEncoding` and `contentMediaType` on the instance being a string. So an integer part carrying `contentEncoding` rides as text/plain carrying the value's own text, and does not take the encoded-string row, an octet boundary this revision does not define, or a refusal no edition states. The `sample` part's own Content-Type header is deliberately not asserted: a text/plain part may carry the header explicitly or omit it, and [RFC7578] Section 4.4 makes both the same wire fact — the reason OAPI-PS-55 declines the same assertion. What IS asserted is that the part carries the value's own text rather than an encoded-string or octet body, and that the sibling `note` part, which declares `type: string` with the same `contentEncoding`, still takes the encoded-string row and still carries the Content-Transfer-Encoding header JSON Schema 2020-12 derives that keyword from.

info.title: Inert content keywords on a declared non-string part

scenarios.description: The whole OAS 3.0 line emits ONE body for a control-free urlencoded property, and this scenario is edition 3.0.0 of the five that state it. The Encoding Object writes contentType and no style, explode or allowReserved, so the content path governs: the object's JSON image rides as one field under the property's own name, with its space spelled + by RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1. Edition 3.0.0 states no lane-selection rule of its own; it reaches this behaviour through its own Section 4.1 patch-uniformity instruction together with 3.0.4, a 3.0.* version, whose Section 4.7.15.1.2 states that with all three fields absent "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone". A processor that keys any part of this on the PATCH component of the openapi field emits address's members as top-level fields (street=main%20st), discards the artifact's explicit contentType, and loses the field name the operation is built around; each of 3.0.0 through 3.0.3 forbids that distinction in its OWN Section 4.1, in the words "The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example" — 3.0.4 and the 3.1 editions carry the same sentence naming 3.1.0 and 3.1.1 instead, so the instruction governing an artifact that declares a 3.0-line patch is the one in that artifact's own edition. One permitted observation, not a set.

info.title: Form content path across the 3.0 line

expected.description: The emitted body under edition 3.0.0. It is byte-identical in all five 3.0-line scenarios, OAPI-PS-60 through OAPI-PS-64.
